hypothesis: Distribute existing distance upper-bound supervision to every violating coordinate instead of relying on only the current max. This preserves all exact Linf solutions and assigns no coordinate identities.
penalty: Mean squared relu(|Q_i(s)-Q_i(g)|-d(s,g)) over the same pairs and all coordinates. No extra truth labels; the max-distance Huber still penalizes underestimation and overestimation.
selection: Both conditions select by complete training hard-Linf distance Huber; infer and evaluate using the unchanged hard maximum. Report best and last, with no test selection.
scope: Same finite-map starting checkpoint, new Adam, labels and training budget. Tests a gradient-distribution mechanism, not a global training solution.
